newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to release Palestinian women prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Israel to release Palestinian women prisoners.

text.p: Israel said it would release on Tuesday 31 female Palestinian prisoners, including women involved in attacks against Jews, as part of its peace agreements with the PLO.
A PLO official said most of the freed prisoners would be taken from prison to the West Bank city of Ramallah, where Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would welcome them.
"Thirty-one Palestinian women will be released today, 25 from Hasharon prison and six from Naveh Tirza prison," an Israeli police spokeswoman said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, paying hospital visits in the north to soldiers wounded in Lebanon, said the promise to free the women -- two of whom were convicted of murder -- was made originally by the previous Labour government.
"It's not a tactic, we are serious about fulfilling commitments, but we intend fully to see that there is an equal reciprocity on the other side," Netanyahu told reporters.

Israel has demanded the PLO keep its promise to change sections of its charter calling for the destruction of the Jewish state, avoid political activity in Jerusalem and fight Palestinian guerrilla groups opposed to peace deals.

Right-wing critics led by Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi called the decision to free the women immoral. The "Families of Victims of Arab Terror" group failed on Monday to persuade Israel's High Court to prevent the release.

"Freeing terrorist-murderers is really difficult and truly painful from a moral point of view...but sometimes it is a political necessity for a different and better future for both sides," said left-wing legislator Yossi Sarid.

PLO official Hisham Abdel Razek told Reuters that after the release one female Palestinian prisoner would remain behind bars in Israel -- a 15-year-old arrested only two weeks ago after attempting to stab an Israeli soldier.
"We will continue to demand her release," Abdel Razek, head of the prisoners' committee of the Palestinian Authority, said in Gaza.
Abdel-Razek said 28 of the women were convicted by Israeli courts of security offences and three were jailed for criminal activity unrelated to the Israel-Arab conflict.

One of the prisoners, Lamya Maarouf, 32, a Brazilian citizen, was arrested in 1986 for driving a car in which Israeli soldier David Manos was kidnapped. Manos was killed and Maarouf was sentenced to 25 years in jail.
Abeer al-Wheidy, 27, was arrested in 1992 for belonging to a cell of the PLO's mainstream Fatah faction which killed a Jewish settler from the settlement of Ofra near Ramallah.
May Ghussein, 23, was arrested in 1991 for security reasons. She confessed to killing a Palestinian in jail suspected of collaborating with the prison authorities.

The release of female, sick and young prisoners was a commitment made in a deal signed by the previous government in September 1995 with the Palestine Liberation Organisation. Israel released some of the male sick and elderly prisoners but some 5,000 Palestinians are still in its prisons.

Israeli President Ezer Weizman at first refused to pardon some of the women who were involved in deadly attacks against Israelis. The female prisoners whom he did pardon then chose to remain in prison in solidarity with their comrades.
An Israeli cabinet statement on Friday said the president had now decided to pardon all of the women.
In a deal with the PLO in January under which Israeli troops withdrew from 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron, Netanyahu pledged to carry out the prisoner releases.
